hints: Look first at the type of starting molecule, since haloalkanes and carbonyl compounds react by completely different mechanisms.
Remember that aldehydes like propanal undergo addition to the C=O bond, with cyanide ion, $\text{CN}^-$, acting as the nucleophile.
Think about how pH affects the concentration of that nucleophile, and whether acid or alkali will help produce more of it for a good yield.
walkthrough:
**Sort by functional group**

Haloalkanes like 1-bromopropane and 2-iodopropane do substitution or elimination, not addition. Only carbonyl compounds like propanal can do nucleophilic addition.

So focus on: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Recall how HCN adds**

HCN itself is a weak acid and a poor nucleophile. The real nucleophile is the cyanide ion, $\text{CN}^-$.

First step is attack on the slightly positive carbonyl carbon:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(O}^-\text{)CN}$$

**Choose conditions for good yield**

Alkaline conditions provide $\text{OH}^-$ which deprotonates HCN to make plenty of $\text{CN}^-$:
$$\text{HCN} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CN}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Acidic conditions do the opposite, they suppress ionisation so almost no $\text{CN}^-$ is present and the reaction is very slow with poor yield. So nucleophilic addition with good yield needs alkaline conditions.

options.A: Hot ethanolic NaOH with a primary haloalkane causes elimination (dehydrohalogenation) to form propene. This is an elimination mechanism, not nucleophilic addition.
options.B: Hot aqueous NaOH with 2-iodopropane causes nucleophilic substitution to form propan-2-ol. This is substitution by $\text{OH}^-$, not addition to a C=O bond.
options.C: Propanal is an aldehyde so $\text{CN}^-$ adds to the C=O bond by nucleophilic addition to give 2-hydroxybutanenitrile. Alkaline conditions generate a high concentration of the $\text{CN}^-$ nucleophile, giving a fast reaction and good yield.
options.D: The mechanism would still be nucleophilic addition in principle, but acid suppresses formation of $\text{CN}^-$ from HCN. With almost no nucleophile present the yield is very poor, so the stated conditions fail the question.
